name: THOME The Glow Signature
editorialDescription: A Korean ultrasound skincare device that you glide over skin with a gel or ampoule for about 12 minutes. THOME, run by athome Co., Ltd., sells it at Sephora in the US, and the design won a Red Dot award. The brand describes dual-frequency ultrasound with three modes. It doesn't use light, and we found no FDA 510(k) record for it, so its performance claims rest on the company's own data.
keyFeatures: Ultrasound device; THOME's US launch materials describe 3MHz + 10MHz dual-frequency ultrasound
Three modes named by the brand: Focus (radiance), Inner (hydration) and Tension (elasticity)
About 12 minutes per session, used with THOME's Boost Ampoule or another conductive gel
137g body with an angled head; retailer listings give a 3.7V 1400mAh rechargeable battery
Described as fully waterproof for cleaning in its Red Dot design award entry
advantages: Comes from an established brand with mainstream US retail (Sephora), and the Amazon seller (athome corporation) matches the company behind THOME
Lightweight, cordless and waterproof, so it's easy to clean
A mode-based design keeps the routine simple
disadvantages: Performance claims, including the brand's 'up to 1900%' heat-shock-protein figure and firming wording, come from company data we couldn't independently verify
No FDA 510(k) record found; it is sold as a cosmetic device
Needs a gel or ampoule every session, which is an ongoing cost
Premium-priced in a category with little independent research
The official site (thome.kr) is in Korean, so English specifications come from retailers and press materials
suits: People who enjoy a device-based massage step and already use serums or gels
Anyone who wants a waterproof, easy-to-clean tool
skipIf: You want a device with FDA clearance or independent clinical evidence behind its claims
You are pregnant, have an implanted electronic device or have irritated or broken skin in the area; read the manual's cautions and ask a clinician first
buyingConsiderations: Check that the seller is THOME's own Amazon store (athome corporation)
Make sure an English manual is included and read the cautions before first use
Treat 'firm-looking', 'glass glow' and percentage figures as marketing
Factor in the cost of Boost Ampoules or a compatible gel

researchNotes: Verified 2026-10-12. Amazon listing B0GYNSM48X is sold by athome corporation and showed In Stock. No 510(k) record found in openFDA for THOME or athome. Ultrasound frequencies and modes come from THOME's press release and retailer listings (Style Korean, Shilla Duty Free); the battery figure is from a retailer listing. The '1900%' heat-shock-protein claim is mentioned only as a claim to be cautious about.
